The name encourages the bearer to embrace their inner power and lead a virtuous and righteous life, just as a ruler leads her people with wisdom and compassion. historical_references.reference: Raji was a queen of the Chalukya dynasty in the Deccan plateau of India, who ruled in the second half of the 11th century. She is best known for her victory over the northern Chalukya king, Bhima I, which allowed her to extend her domain further north.

Another Raji was a queen of the Haihaiyas, a minor ruling dynasty in the eastern part of the Deccan plateau of India, who lived in the late 16th century. She is best known for her successful resistance against the invading Mughal forces under the command of Akbar, during which she is said to have killed Akbar's general, Malik Ambar, in a battle.
